verdict.rationale: GoDaddy's docs confirm DNS hosting on its authoritative nameservers. Records can be created, read, replaced and deleted via the API and via the gddy CLI (e.g. `gddy dns set --type A`), so the core of DNS hosting with the domain is delivered. However, there is no evidence on which record types are supported or on minimum TTLs, and one hands-on community report says the domain management interface is very slow. That undercuts the 'UI that doesn't fight me' part of the story. Missing for 10: documented list of supported record types (e.g. CAA, SRV, ALIAS), minimum TTL values, evidence of a good web management UI, and independent corroboration of DNS quality.
